extra.message: The FastAPI application is instantiated with no authentication of any kind: no auth middleware, route dependencies, API keys, or session handling are configured anywhere in the app. Every route (GET /select, PUT /user, GET/POST /find, DELETE /user, POST /reset) exposes reading, creating and deleting all user records to any unauthenticated network client.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: In run_sql_query(), when the query returns more than one row the raw tuples of 'SELECT *' are returned verbatim via {'users': _data}, including the password column (index 3). The single-row path (lines 151-161) deliberately excludes the password field, but the multi-row path leaks MD5 password hashes, e.g. via GET /select with a filter matching multiple users or via SQL injection.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The 'username' query parameter of GET /select is interpolated directly into the SQL statement f'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";', which is executed by run_sql_query() (db.execute at line 146). An attacker can escape the double-quoted value (e.g. username=\" OR 1=1; -- ) to read, modify or destroy the entire users table via SQL injection.

User-supplied passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (md5(user.password.encode()).hexdigest()); the seeded users are hashed identically at main.py:113. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted hashes are trivially reversed with rainbow tables or fast brute force, so any leaked hash (see the multi-row leak at line 162) reveals the original password. A salted slow KDF (bcrypt/scrypt/argon2) should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: PUT /user builds the INSERT statement by f-string interpolation of the attacker-controlled User model fields (\"{user.name}\", \"{user.username}\", \"{user.address}\", \"{user.email}\", \"{user.contact}\" at lines 197-202) instead of parameterized queries. Any field containing a double quote breaks out of the SQL string literal, allowing arbitrary SQL injection (e.g. inserting extra rows, corrupting or dropping the users table) via the JSON request body.

POST /find takes the raw JSON request body (await request.json()) and passes it directly as the MongoDB/MontyDB query filter to get_nosql_users() -> users.find(query) with no validation or operator sanitization. An attacker can inject query operators such as {\"username\": {\"$ne\": \"\"}} or {\"id\": {\"$in\": [1, 2]}} to bypass the intended filter and dump every user document in the collection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The DELETE /user endpoint performs destructive deletion of arbitrary user records (both SQL and NoSQL stores) with no authorization check of any kind. Any unauthenticated remote client can erase any user's account simply by supplying a username; combined with the SQL injection at line 231, the whole users table can be wiped.

DELETE /user interpolates the attacker-controlled 'username' parameter directly into f'DELETE FROM users WHERE username = "{username}";' without parameterization. An attacker can terminate the quoted value and inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. username=\" OR 1=1; --) to delete every row in the users table.

DELETE /user interpolates user.address from the request body into the SQL statement without even surrounding quotes: f'DELETE FROM users WHERE address = {user.address};'. Because the value is not inside a string literal, any SQL syntax supplied in the 'address' field (e.g. '1 OR 1=1') is executed directly, making arbitrary SQL injection trivial.

POST /reset deletes and reinitializes the application's databases (remove() of the SQLite file, rmtree() of the NoSQL store, then init_db()) with no authentication or authorization. Any remote client can issue this request at will to destroy all persisted data, causing permanent data loss and a denial-of-service condition for every other user.
